{"body":"Sub-issue of #820. Backend half of the test-suite cleanup: dedupe overlapping
coverage, retire dead-weight migration tests, and fix the per-test DB setup
cost that dominates runtime.

## Findings

**Overlap / duplication**

- `test_merge.py` and `test_merge_preview.py` both exercise
  `app.services.merge.merge_trees`; `test_merge_preview.py` was added
  "in addition to" `test_merge.py` "to verify backward compatibility"
  (see its header comment) rather than folding the old cases in — basic
  dedupe/merge behavior (e.g. `test_merge_dedupes_identical_members` in
  `test_merge.py`) is effectively re-covered by the resolution-aware variants.
- `test_friends.py::test_unfriend_revokes_shared_trees_both_directions` and
  `::test_block_prevents_requests_and_revokes_shares` assert the same
  `TreeMembership` deletion behavior that `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py`
  (`test_unfriend_revokes_both_directions`,
  `test_block_emits_access_changed_and_notification`) already covers, plus SSE
  assertions.
- An identical `owner`/`tree`/`headers` fixture trio is copy-pasted
  (byte-for-byte) into at least `test_activity_events.py`,
  `test_content_events.py`, `test_layout_events.py`, `test_presence.py`, and
  `test_storage_warning_events.py` instead of living in `conftest.py`.
- `test_global_search.py::test_global_search_matches_name_permutation_and_birth_year`
  and `::test_global_search_matches_death_year_the_same_way_as_birth_year` are
  structurally identical (the second name literally says "the same way as") —
  a `@pytest.mark.parametrize` candidate.
- `test_storage.py` has near-identical buffered-vs-streamed pairs (e.g.
  `test_oversized_payload_raises_image_too_large` /
  `test_streamed_oversized_image_rejected_and_temp_removed`, and the same
  pattern for unsupported-mime and bad-dimensions cases) — legitimate coverage
  of parallel code paths, but parametrizing would cut ~150 lines of
  near-duplicate bodies.

**Low-value / obsolete**

- `test_remove_announcement_settings_migration.py`,
  `test_research_task_links_migration.py`, and `test_documents_migration.py`
  (~400+ lines combined) pin one-off Alembic data migrations
  (`v1_7_0_release.py`, `v1_8_0_research_task_links.py`) that only matter to
  instances upgrading through that specific version. Once a version has
  shipped past a couple of releases, this code path is effectively
  unreachable but keeps being verified forever.

**Setup/infra**

- `conftest.py` creates a **fresh on-disk SQLite file per test**
  (`create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path/'test.db'}")` +
  `Base.metadata.create_all()`), not an in-memory DB or a
  transaction-rollback strategy. `--durations` shows the slowest entries are
  almost all fixture **setup** time (1.5–2.3s each), not test-body time.
- `test_event_bus_redis.py` uses real `asyncio.sleep(0.1–0.3)` calls (multiple
  call sites) to let a background listener task catch up — slow and a
  potential source of flakiness under load, unlike `test_geocoding.py` which
  correctly monkeypatches `time.sleep`.
- Good news: factory helpers (`make_user`, `make_tree`, `share`, `add_member`,
  `befriend`, `auth`, `wait_for_job`) are already defined once and reused
  across 60+ files — the boilerplate problem is narrower than it could be.

**Runtime**: serial `uv run pytest -q` — **18m32s wall / 5m40s user / 0m27s
sys** for ~1016 tests. CI's `-n auto` masks this; local/serial runs and any
non-xdist runner pay the full cost.

## Scope

- [ ] Consolidate `test_merge.py` / `test_merge_preview.py` overlap (keep one
      canonical set of dedupe assertions).
- [ ] Remove the duplicated `TreeMembership`-revocation assertions from
      `test_friends.py` that `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py` already covers
      (or vice versa — keep whichever file is the better home).
- [ ] Hoist the copy-pasted `owner`/`tree`/`headers` fixture trio into
      `conftest.py`; update the five files that redefine it locally.
- [ ] Parametrize the `test_global_search.py` name/birth-year vs. death-year
      pair and the `test_storage.py` buffered/streamed pairs.
- [ ] Decide and apply a retention policy for migration-data tests (e.g.
      archive/delete tests for migrations more than N releases old) and apply
      it to the three migration test files above.
- [ ] Replace the per-test on-disk SQLite file + full `create_all()` in
      `conftest.py` with a faster strategy (in-memory SQLite with
      `StaticPool`, or a session-scoped engine + per-test transaction
      rollback) and measure the wall-time improvement.
- [ ] Replace the real `asyncio.sleep()` polling in `test_event_bus_redis.py`
      with a deterministic wait (event/condition) instead of fixed sleeps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest` still passes with no loss of meaningful behavioral
      coverage.
- [ ] Serial `uv run pytest -q` wall time is measurably reduced from the
      ~18m32s baseline above (report the new number in the PR).
- [ ] `uv run ruff check` passes.

193	    """Build a minimal valid PNG of the given dimensions."""
194	
195	    def chunk(name: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
196	        raw = name + data
197	        crc = zlib.crc32(raw) & 0xFFFFFFFF
198	        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + raw + struct.pack(">I", crc)
199	
200	    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
201	    raw_row = b"\x00" + b"\xff\x00\x00" * width
202	    raw_rows = raw_row * height
203	    idat = zlib.compress(raw_rows)
204	    return (
205	        b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
206	        + chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr)
207	        + chunk(b"IDAT", idat)
208	        + chunk(b"IEND", b"")
209	    )

async def _until(predicate, timeout: float = 2.0) -> None:
    """Poll ``predicate`` every tick until true, or raise after ``timeout``.

    Deterministic replacement for fixed ``asyncio.sleep()`` waits: yields
    control so the listener/background task can advance, without pinning the
    test to a specific real-time delay.
    """
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    deadline = loop.time() + timeout
    while not predicate():
        if loop.time() >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError(f"condition not met within {timeout}s")
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

## Code Review — PR #837: Backend test-suite cleanup (#821)

### Overview
This PR addresses issue #821 (backend half of the test-suite cleanup): switches the per-test SQLite fixture from an on-disk file to an in-memory `StaticPool` database, hoists a duplicated fixture trio into `conftest.py`, removes two genuinely-duplicate assertions (merge, friends/unfriend), parametrizes two near-identical test pairs (global search, storage upload rejection), replaces fixed `asyncio.sleep()` waits with deterministic ones in the Redis event-bus tests, and documents (without applying) a migration-test retention policy. - **`StaticPool` in-memory DB** (`conftest.py`): this is the well-established FastAPI/SQLAlchemy pattern for SQLite test doubles — one shared connection across the test's `db`, `client`, and background-job sessions, recreated fresh per test via the function-scoped `session_factory` fixture, so cross-test isolation is preserved (each test gets its own engine/connection, torn down via `engine.dispose()`). Verified empirically: full 1015-test suite green, and `test_event_bus_redis.py` run 8x with no flakiness.
- **Merge/friends dedup**: the removed tests (`test_merge_no_resolutions_backward_compat`, `test_unfriend_revokes_shared_trees_both_directions`) are byte-for-byte equivalent in assertion to tests kept elsewhere — confirmed by diff comparison. No coverage loss.
- **Parametrize refactors** preserve every original case (verified: storage.py's collapsed functions produce the same 8 parametrized instances; global_search's split preserves both original query/assertion pairs, net +1 test from splitting the permutation check out).
- **Event-bus determinism**: the sentinel-message technique in `test_redis_listener_ignores_unknown_channels` correctly exploits FIFO delivery order to prove the two bad messages were skipped rather than relying on wall-clock margin — a solid fix.

### Code quality / style
- Comments are appropriately sparse and explain *why* (e.g., the `StaticPool` docstring note, the sentinel-ordering rationale) rather than restating the diff.
- The `_until()` helper is a small, reusable, well-documented polling primitive scoped to the one file that needs it.
- Migration-test retention comments are consistent and correctly reflect the repo's actual version state (1.8 current / 1.7 prior) — a good call to defer deletion rather than force the issue's literal checkbox, and it's clearly explained in the PR body.

### Minor nits (non-blocking)
- In `test_storage.py`'s new `test_buffered_upload_rejects`, the `unsupported_mime` case now unconditionally runs `monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "DATA_PATH", tmp_path)` even though that case never touches disk (the original standalone test took no `tmp_path`/`monkeypatch` args at all). Harmless — `store_data_url` rejects on mime type before any I/O — but slightly imprecise; not worth un-parametrizing over.
- `test_friends.py`'s renamed `test_block_gates_requests_and_unblock_restores` no longer touches `TreeMembership`/`share`/`make_tree` at all, which is intentional per the PR description, but worth a reviewer double-checking there isn't a *third* piece of unique behavior in the old test that got silently dropped along with the trim (I didn't find one — the removed assertion was purely the membership-deletion check, which `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py::test_block_emits_access_changed_and_notification` already covers).

### Test coverage
No regression: 1015 tests vs. ~1016 before, with the sole net removal being two verified duplicates. `uv run pytest` and `uv run ruff check` both pass per the PR's stated test plan.

### Security
No security-relevant surface here — this is test-infrastructure-only; no production code paths touched.

### Risk
Low. The main structural change (in-memory SQLite via `StaticPool`) is a known-good pattern, already validated against the full suite. The dedup/parametrize changes are mechanical and diff-verifiable. The only latent risk is future tests that assume separate/isolated DB connections within a single test (e.g., testing true connection-level isolation) — none currently exist, but worth keeping in mind if such a test is added later.

**Verdict: no blocking issues found.** Ready to merge as-is.

## Summary

Closes #822. Frontend half of the test-suite cleanup: dedupe component tests that re-run store logic a second time via *Service mocks, and hoist the copy-pasted test setup into one shared place.

- **`src/test/setup.ts`**: added the shared `ResizeObserver` mock, `scrollIntoView`/pointer-capture polyfills, and a global `i18n.changeLanguage("en")` `beforeEach` (the app defaults to "de" outside a stored preference, which is why every file was re-asserting "en"). Removed the now-redundant per-file copies from all affected files — 9 for `ResizeObserver`, 12 for `scrollIntoView`, 8 for pointer-capture, 37 for the i18n init.
- **`src/test/utils.tsx`**: new `renderWithProviders` helper. This app needs almost no test-time providers — i18n and Zustand are module-level singletons, not React context — so the helper is a thin, opt-in wrapper whose only real job is `ReactFlowProvider` for the one component that reads React Flow context. Migrated 3 reference tests (`SelectionModeController`, `ActivityView`, `MemberDocuments`) to demonstrate the pattern.
- **Store-vs-service mocking**: verified each of the issue's flagged files against its actual source (several of the issue's findings didn't hold up — `MergeMembersDialog` and `LinkExistingTreeDialog` already mock the store correctly, `LegalVersionHistoryPanel`/`AdminAuditPanel` have no store layer to mock, `MemberDocuments`'s service mock was just a stray unused line). The two genuine cases (`ImageSheet`, `MemberPhotos`) now mock `useGalleryStore`'s actions instead of `TreeService`, backed by existing `useGalleryStore.test.ts` coverage.

Added store-level tests for all 12 thin `run(treeId, () => TreeSharingService.x(...))` wrappers *first*, then migrated the component test to mock the store — so no behavioral coverage is lost in the process.
- Parametrized `FamilyNodeContent.test.tsx`'s 4 date/deceased-driven tests with `it.each`.

{"body":"> **Epic.** The test suites have grown large enough that they're worth a
> critical pass, not just more additions. Split into a frontend and a backend
> sub-issue since the causes and fixes differ per stack; this issue tracks the
> shared goal and cross-cutting findings.

## Why

- **Backend**: 74 `test_*.py` files, ~20.8k lines, ~1016 tests. A full serial
  `uv run pytest` run takes **~18m32s wall** (vs 5m40s user/0m27s sys — the gap
  is disk I/O, not CPU), because `conftest.py` creates a fresh on-disk SQLite
  file + full `Base.metadata.create_all()` **per test**. CI's `-n auto`
  parallelism hides this, but local/serial runs and any non-xdist CI runner pay
  the full cost.
- **Frontend**: 111 `*.test.ts(x)` files, ~16.9k lines, 736 tests. Runtime itself
  is healthy (~35s total, no pathological tests), but `src/test/setup.ts` is 2
  lines and does nothing beyond importing `jest-dom` — every file hand-rolls its
  own `ResizeObserver` polyfill, i18n init, and render wrapper instead of
  sharing one.
- In both stacks there's real duplication: tests re-verifying the same behavior
  across multiple files/layers, and some tests (backend data-migration tests,
  frontend component tests that re-run store logic instead of mocking the
  store) that are candidates to trim, consolidate, or parametrize.

This isn't about hitting a target test count — it's about cutting redundant
coverage and shared-setup boilerplate so the suites stay fast and easy to
extend as the app grows.

## Plan (sub-issues)

1. **Backend** — dedupe overlapping tests, retire/archive one-off migration
   tests, hoist copy-pasted fixtures into `conftest.py`, fix the per-test SQLite
   file creation that dominates runtime.
2. **Frontend** — dedupe store-vs-component re-testing, hoist the copy-pasted
   `ResizeObserver` mock / i18n init / render boilerplate into `src/test/setup.ts`
   (+ a shared `renderWithProviders` helper), parametrize near-duplicate tests.

Both sub-issues are independent and can be worked in parallel.

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

- [ ] Backend: identified duplicate/overlapping tests are consolidated or
      removed with no loss of behavioral coverage; shared fixtures are hoisted
      into `conftest.py`; serial `pytest` wall time is measurably reduced.
- [ ] Frontend: identified duplicate/overlapping tests are consolidated;
      shared test setup (ResizeObserver, i18n, render helper) lives in one
      place instead of being copy-pasted per file.
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npx vitest run`, `uv run ruff check`, and `uv run pytest`
      all still pass green.
- [ ] No net loss of meaningful behavioral coverage — this is about removing
      redundancy and cutting setup cost, not weakening the suite.

Sub-issue of #820. E2E half of the test-suite cleanup: dedupe hand-rolled
per-file helpers that duplicate what the shared Playwright fixtures already
provide, and replace fixed-delay waits with deterministic ones.

## Findings

**Overlap / duplication**

- `tests/tree-lifecycle.spec.ts::loginAs(page, user)` and
  `tests/members-canvas.spec.ts::login(page, user)` are each a standalone
  reimplementation of the exact login flow (`fill #username` / `fill
  #password` / submit / wait for the form to disappear) that
  `fixtures/index.ts`'s `adminPage` fixture already performs — just
  parameterized to accept an arbitrary `user` instead of the hardcoded admin.
  Neither file reuses the fixture or a shared helper; the same ~8 lines are
  copy-pasted three times (including the inline block inside `adminPage`
  itself).
- `tests/tree-lifecycle.spec.ts::selectTree(page, name)` and
  `tests/views.spec.ts::selectTree(page, name)` are two independent
  implementations of "open the tree selector and pick an option by name" —
  near-identical but not identical (`views.spec.ts`'s version skips
  re-selecting if the tree is already active and asserts the selector's text
  afterward; `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts`'s does not). Worth reconciling into one
  shared helper in `fixtures/` rather than two spec-local, subtly divergent
  copies.
- `tests/smoke.spec.ts` (harness self-checks: "programmatic login returns a
  valid access token", "adminPage fixture yields an authenticated session",
  "app shell loads and shows login page when unauthenticated") overlaps in
  spirit with `tests/auth.spec.ts::"login success — valid credentials land on
  the authenticated layout"`. This may be intentional (smoke tests validate
  the harness itself, not app behavior) — confirm intent before trimming
  either side; if smoke.spec.ts is meant as a fixture/harness sanity check
  rather than app-behavior coverage, say so with a comment so the next reader
  doesn't mistake it for redundant coverage.

**Fixed waits**

- `tests/views.spec.ts` has three `page.waitForTimeout(...)` calls (2000ms,
  2000ms, 1000ms) — real-time sleeps rather than waiting on a specific DOM
  state or network response. These are slow and a potential source of
  flakiness under load, the same category of issue fixed for the backend's
  `test_event_bus_redis.py` in #821.

**Setup/infra**

- `fixtures/index.ts` is already in good shape — `adminApi`, `adminPage`,
  `secondUser`, `secondApi`, and `seedTree` are shared, documented fixtures
  reused across all 9 spec files via `test.extend`, and the page-level i18n
  pin / tutorial-dismiss / SSE-abort / What's-New-ack routes are centralized
  there rather than copy-pasted. This suite does not have the "2-line
  setup.ts" problem the frontend had — the fixture layer is the right
  reference pattern; the two `login`/`selectTree` duplicates above are the
  exception, not the norm.
- Runtime was not measured in this pass (the full stack needs
  `docker-compose.e2e.yml` up to run the suite) — this issue is scoped to the
  duplication/fixed-wait findings above, not a proven speed problem. If
  runtime turns out to be an issue once measured, treat that as a separate
  finding rather than assuming it here.

## Scope

- [ ] Hoist a single `loginAs(page, user)` helper into `fixtures/` (or extend
      the existing fixture set with a parameterized login fixture) and have
      `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts` and `members-canvas.spec.ts` use it instead of
      their own copies; keep `adminPage`'s convenience for the common
      admin-login case.
- [ ] Hoist a single `selectTree(page, name)` helper into `fixtures/`,
      reconciling the two current implementations (decide which behavior —
      e.g. the already-selected skip + post-selection assertion in
      `views.spec.ts` — is correct and keep that), and update both spec files
      to use it.
- [ ] Replace the three `page.waitForTimeout(...)` calls in `views.spec.ts`
      with waits on the actual condition being awaited (a locator becoming
      visible/stable, a network response, etc.).
- [ ] Confirm whether `smoke.spec.ts`'s auth-adjacent checks are intentional
      harness self-checks distinct from `auth.spec.ts`'s app-behavior
      coverage; if so, document that with a short comment, otherwise trim the
      genuine duplicate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Playwright suite (`npx playwright test` against the
      `docker-compose.e2e.yml` stack) still passes with no loss of meaningful
      behavioral coverage.
- [ ] No spec file hand-rolls its own login or tree-selection helper — both
      live once in `fixtures/`.
- [ ] No fixed-delay `waitForTimeout` remains in `views.spec.ts` (or anywhere
      it can be replaced with a deterministic wait).

input.command:
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/e820_body.md
> **Epic.** The test suites have grown large enough that they're worth a
> critical pass, not just more additions. Split into a frontend and a backend
> sub-issue since the causes and fixes differ per stack; this issue tracks the
> shared goal and cross-cutting findings.

## Why

- **Backend**: 74 `test_*.py` files, ~20.8k lines, ~1016 tests. A full serial
  `uv run pytest` run takes **~18m32s wall** (vs 5m40s user/0m27s sys — the gap
  is disk I/O, not CPU), because `conftest.py` creates a fresh on-disk SQLite
  file + full `Base.metadata.create_all()` **per test**. CI's `-n auto`
  parallelism hides this, but local/serial runs and any non-xdist CI runner pay
  the full cost.
- **Frontend**: 111 `*.test.ts(x)` files, ~16.9k lines, 736 tests. Runtime itself
  is healthy (~35s total, no pathological tests), but `src/test/setup.ts` is 2
  lines and does nothing beyond importing `jest-dom` — every file hand-rolls its
  own `ResizeObserver` polyfill, i18n init, and render wrapper instead of
  sharing one.
- **E2E**: 9 `*.spec.ts` files, ~3.1k lines, 74 tests. The fixture layer
  (`fixtures/index.ts`) is already in good shape, but a couple of spec files
  hand-roll their own login/tree-selection helpers instead of reusing it, and
  one file uses fixed-delay `waitForTimeout` calls instead of deterministic
  waits.
- In both stacks there's real duplication: tests re-verifying the same behavior
  across multiple files/layers, and some tests (backend data-migration tests,
  frontend component tests that re-run store logic instead of mocking the
  store) that are candidates to trim, consolidate, or parametrize.

This isn't about hitting a target test count — it's about cutting redundant
coverage and shared-setup boilerplate so the suites stay fast and easy to
extend as the app grows.

## Plan (sub-issues)

1. **Backend** (#821) — dedupe overlapping tests, retire/archive one-off
   migration tests, hoist copy-pasted fixtures into `conftest.py`, fix the
   per-test SQLite file creation that dominates runtime.
2. **Frontend** (#822) — dedupe store-vs-component re-testing, hoist the
   copy-pasted `ResizeObserver` mock / i18n init / render boilerplate into
   `src/test/setup.ts` (+ a shared `renderWithProviders` helper), parametrize
   near-duplicate tests.
3. **E2E** (#839) — dedupe hand-rolled login/tree-selection helpers that
   duplicate the shared Playwright fixtures, replace fixed-delay waits with
   deterministic ones.

All three sub-issues are independent and can be worked in parallel.

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

- [x] Backend: identified duplicate/overlapping tests are consolidated or
      removed with no loss of behavioral coverage; shared fixtures are hoisted
      into `conftest.py`; serial `pytest` wall time is measurably reduced.
      (#821)
- [x] Frontend: identified duplicate/overlapping tests are consolidated;
      shared test setup (ResizeObserver, i18n, render helper) lives in one
      place instead of being copy-pasted per file. (#822)
- [ ] E2E: hand-rolled per-file helpers are consolidated into the shared
      fixture layer; fixed-delay waits are replaced with deterministic ones.
      (#839)
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npx vitest run`, `uv run ruff check`, `uv run pytest`,
      and the Playwright E2E suite all still pass green.
- [ ] No net loss of meaningful behavioral coverage — this is about removing
      redundancy and cutting setup cost, not weakening the suite.
EOF

gh pr create --title "test(e2e): dedupe hand-rolled helpers, replace fixed waits" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Closes #839. E2E half of the test-suite cleanup: dedupe hand-rolled per-file login/tree-selection helpers that duplicate the shared Playwright fixtures, and replace fixed-delay waits with deterministic ones.

- **New `e2e/fixtures/ui.ts`**: hoists `loginAs` (previously duplicated 3x — the inline block in `fixtures/index.ts`'s `adminPage`, `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts::loginAs`, `members-canvas.spec.ts::login`) and `selectTree` (previously duplicated 2x, in `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts` and `views.spec.ts`) into one place.
  - `members-canvas.spec.ts` keeps its `login` name but as a thin wrapper: `loginAs` + the file-specific "Family tree canvas" visible assertion, since `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts`'s empty-tree test has no canvas to wait for and shouldn't be forced through that gate.
  - The shared `selectTree` keeps `views.spec.ts`'s superset behavior (skip re-selecting if the tree is already active); confirmed `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts`'s call sites never depend on the skip's absence.
- **`views.spec.ts`**: replaced its three `page.waitForTimeout(...)` calls (2000ms gallery, 2000ms map, 1000ms quality report) with waits on the actual condition:
  - Gallery: wait for the "No photos yet" empty state instead of a fixed delay.
  - Map: wait for `.leaflet-container` to mount.
  - Quality report: removed the sleep outright — the existing `waitForLoadState("networkidle")` + heading assertion already gated on render completion, so it was dead weight.
- **`smoke.spec.ts`**: added a comment clarifying its auth-adjacent tests ("programmatic login returns a valid access token", "adminPage fixture yields an authenticated session") are intentional harness self-checks — distinct from `auth.spec.ts`'s app-behavior coverage — so a future reader doesn't mistake them for redundant and delete them.

**Verification — against the real stack, not just statically.** `e2e/` has no separate CI-runnable check outside the full `docker-compose.e2e.yml` stack, so I built and ran it locally: full baseline run before any changes (**73 passed, 2 pre-existing skips, ~49.5s**), then the identical **73 passed, 2 skipped** after all changes, repeated 3x with no flakiness (~47-48s each — slightly faster, since the deterministic waits resolve before their fixed-delay equivalents would have).

One of the plan's proposed replacements turned out to be wrong when checked against the live app: the "quality report" test's comment claims a member with missing dates "should trigger a quality flag," but the app actually renders "No issues found" for that seed data — asserting the flagged name would have been a false assertion. Left the existing (correct) assertions in place there rather than adding one I'd verified doesn't hold; not fixing that pre-existing test-comment/behavior mismatch since it's outside this issue's scope.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx playwright test --list` — same 75 tests enumerated before/after (no titles changed)
- [x] Full suite run against `docker-compose.e2e.yml`: baseline 73 passed / 2 skipped (~49.5s) → after 73 passed / 2 skipped, run 3x, no flakiness
- [x] `grep` confirms no spec file still hand-rolls a full `login`/`loginAs`/`selectTree` implementation
- [x] No `waitForTimeout` remains anywhere in `e2e/tests/`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1

content.text:
## Code Review — PR #840: E2E suite cleanup (#839)

### Overview
Hoists three duplicated login-flow implementations and two duplicated tree-selector implementations into a new `e2e/fixtures/ui.ts`, replaces three fixed-delay `waitForTimeout()` calls in `views.spec.ts` with waits on the actual settling condition, and documents `smoke.spec.ts`'s intentional overlap with `auth.spec.ts`. Small, surgical diff (80 additions / 58 deletions across 6 files).

### Correctness
- **`loginAs` extraction** is behavior-preserving: the canonical version kept is the one with the `#username`-visible pre-check (matching both the old `adminPage` inline block and `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts`'s copy). `members-canvas.spec.ts`'s extra `"Family tree canvas"` visibility assertion was correctly kept as a local wrapper rather than folded into the shared helper — pushing it into `loginAs` would have broken `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts`'s empty-tree test, which has no canvas to wait for. Good judgment call, called out explicitly in the PR body.
- **`selectTree` unification** keeps the superset behavior (skip-if-already-selected + post-selection `toContainText` assertion) from `views.spec.ts`. This is strictly more thorough than `tree-lifecycle.spec.ts`'s original version, not less.
- **The `waitForTimeout` replacements are verified against the real DOM**, not guessed — the PR description is explicit that the initial plan's proposed replacement for the quality-report test (asserting a flagged "Incomplete Data" entry) was checked against the live app and found to be false (the app renders "No issues found" for that seed data), so that spot was left with its existing assertions rather than shipping an unverified — and in this case actually incorrect — locator. That's exactly the right call, and it's good that it's surfaced in the PR rather than silently worked around.
- **Verification methodology is the standout here**: rather than relying on `playwright test --list` alone (a static, transpile-only check, since `e2e/` has no tsc/lint step), the actual `docker-compose.e2e.yml` stack was built and run — baseline (73 passed/2 skipped, ~49.5s) captured *before* any change, then the identical result reproduced 3x after, with a modest speed improvement. This is materially stronger evidence than the plan's own fallback assumption ("the implementer likely cannot spin up the stack").

### Code quality / style
- `fixtures/ui.ts` follows the existing fixture-module conventions (JSDoc header explaining scope/rationale, named exports, no default export) consistent with `seed.ts`/`users.ts`/`api.ts`.
- The comment on `members-canvas.spec.ts`'s `login` wrapper is appropriately terse and explains the *why* (canvas gate is file-specific, not universal) rather than restating the diff.
- The `smoke.spec.ts` addition extends the existing top-of-file docblock rather than scattering inline comments across two unrelated tests — the right home for a cross-cutting clarification.
- Comments on the two remaining `views.spec.ts` waits (gallery empty-state, Leaflet mount) state *what condition* is being waited for, matching the codebase's established comment style elsewhere in this file (e.g., the SSE-abort comment in `fixtures/index.ts`).

### Minor observations (non-blocking)
- `LoginCredentials` (the new exported interface in `ui.ts`) is structurally satisfied by `UserRecord` (which has an extra `id` field) at every call site — fine under TypeScript's structural typing, just worth knowing there's no explicit `UserRecord → LoginCredentials` adapter needed.
- The quality-report test's stale comment ("should trigger a quality flag") and title ("members with missing dates are flagged") are now known to not match actual app behavior. Correctly left untouched as out-of-scope for this PR, but worth a follow-up issue since it's a latent test-correctness gap independent of this cleanup.

### Risk
Low. All three touched spec files were run against a live, freshly-built stack multiple times with identical pass/skip counts before and after. The only theoretical residual risk is CI's containerized environment behaving subtly differently from the local Docker build used here (e.g., different Chromium version, different timing characteristics) — but the new waits are all *more* deterministic than what they replaced, and the generous `10_000ms` timeouts are conservative, not tightened.

### Security
No security-relevant surface — test-infrastructure-only changes, no production code touched.

**Verdict: no blocking issues found.** Ready to merge.
